core: Recursion is an algorithmic technique in which a function calls itself with a smaller part of the problem
A recursive definition needs a base case (stops the recursion) and a recursive case (progresses toward the base case)
Each recursive call adds a frame to the call stack; frames are removed when calls return
A missing or unreachable base case causes infinite recursion, which overflows the stack (Python raises RecursionError; default limit 1000)

claims.claim: Recursion is an algorithmic technique where a function, to accomplish a task, calls itself with some part of the task.
A recursive solution has a base case (simple enough to solve directly) and a recursive case (divide into smaller parts, call the function on each, combine results).
If a recursion never reaches a base case, it makes recursive calls forever and the program never terminates (infinite recursion).
Each recursive call adds a frame to the call stack; the base case does not make a recursive call, so no further frames are added, and frames are removed as calls return.
The call stack is a stack: the most recently added item (the active call's frame) is the one removed next (last-in, first-out).

Python's default recursion limit is 1000, and exceeding the interpreter stack depth raises a RecursionError; the limit exists to prevent infinite recursion from overflowing the C stack and crashing the interpreter.

factorial(4) = 4*3*2*1 = 24, and the recursive definition factorial(n) = 1 if n==0 else n*factorial(n-1) computes this by calling factorial five times (n = 4,3,2,1,0) and multiplying on the way back up.
Recursion and iteration are alternative techniques for repeating work; the same computation (e.g., factorial) can be written either as a self-calling function or as a loop with explicit variables.
Recursion is built on functions: a function that calls itself is still an ordinary named sequence of statements that performs a computation and can return a value.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Some sources quote a RecursionError near 3000 frames rather than 1000.
positions: Python's documented default recursion limit is 1000 (sys.getrecursionlimit()).
A specific Think Python run reported roughly 3000 frames before the error, reflecting a raised or version-specific limit.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson states the documented default is 1000 and was verified in Bash (sys.getrecursionlimit() returned 1000); the exact number can be changed with sys.setrecursionlimit(), so the lesson presents 1000 as the default, not a universal constant.

sourceRecords.title: recursion - Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures (DADS)
sourceRecords.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sourceRecords.notes: Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19. Authoritative public-domain definition: 'An algorithmic technique where a function, in order to accomplish a task, calls itself with some part of the task.' Identifies the two components of a recursive solution: base case(s) (simple enough to solve directly) and recursive case(s) (divide the problem, call recursively on each part, combine the solutions). Lists iteration and divide-and-conquer as related. Supports the definition, the base/recursive-case framing, and the iteration contrast. Prose synthesized, not copied.

sourceRecords.title: stack - Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures (DADS)
sourceRecords.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sourceRecords.notes: Reused registry record. Authoritative public-domain definition of a stack: a collection in which only the most recently added item may be removed (last-in, first-out; push and pop). Used only to justify that the call stack behaves as a LIFO stack; stack operations themselves are the owned Stacks topic and are named, not re-taught.

sourceRecords.title: Think Python (3rd ed.), Chapter 5: Conditionals and Recursion
sourceRecords.provider: Allen B. Downey / Green Tea Press
sourceRecords.notes: Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19. Chapter 'Conditionals and Recursion' introduces recursion with a countdown function, defines the base case as the bottom of the stack that makes no recursive call (so no more frames), and states that a recursion that never reaches a base case 'goes on making recursive calls forever, and the program never terminates,' producing a RecursionError ('maximum recursion depth exceeded'). Supports base case, call-stack frames, and infinite recursion. CC BY-NC-SA: original prose only, no wording reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: sys - System-specific parameters and functions (recursion limit)
sourceRecords.notes: Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19 and verified in Bash. sys.getrecursionlimit() returns the maximum depth of the Python interpreter stack; sys.setrecursionlimit() changes it. The documented purpose: the limit 'prevents infinite recursion from causing an overflow of the C stack and crashing Python.' Bash check on this machine: sys.getrecursionlimit() returned 1000, and a base-case-free function raised RecursionError. Supports the default-1000 and RecursionError statements.

sourceRecords.title: Think Python, 2e - Chapter 3: Functions
sourceRecords.provider: Allen B. Downey / Green Tea Press
sourceRecords.notes: Reused registry record. Defines a function as a named sequence of statements that performs a computation and can return a value (fruitful vs void).
